name: System detection efficiency of a NbN superconducting microstrip single-photon detector at 1550 nm at 0.84 K (adsorption refrigerator), with a 2.1 K G-M cryocooler cross-check
plain_name: Test a wide-strip superconducting photon counter below 1 kelvin so it catches over 90% of telecom photons
description: Xu et al. (SIMIT) characterise a fibre-coupled NbN microstrip detector (50 um active diameter) at 0.84 K in an adsorption refrigerator (SDE ~92.2% at 1550 nm) and at 2.1 K in a compact closed-cycle G-M cryocooler (SDE > 70%); biased and read out through a cryogenic coaxial cable and a room-temperature bias tee.
keywords: Test a wide-strip superconducting photon counter below 1 kelvin so it catches over 90% of telecom photons

sources.citation: Superconducting microstrip single-photon detector with system detection efficiency over 90% at 1550 nm (Xu et al., arXiv:2101.05407)

requirements.rationale: The >90% system detection efficiency was obtained at 0.84 K; reaching that temperature is needed to reproduce the headline result.
The detector is DC-biased and its RF pulses are read out through a cryogenic coaxial line to the bias tee.
Optional: the paper also qualifies the detector (SDE > 70%) in a 2.1 K closed-cycle cryocooler, the practical deployment configuration.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
